record.original_question: Let Hd denote the space of holomorphic maps f : P^2 → P^2 of degree d. This is a finite dimensional space parametrized by the coefficients. Does the set of f ∈ Hd with infinitely many attractive basins have measure zero?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.3.7 Let Hd denote the space of holomorphic maps f : P2 → P2 of degree d. This is a finite dimensional space parametrized by the coefficients. Does the set of f ∈ Hd with infinitely many attractive basins have measure zero?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\ge 2$, let $\mathcal{H}_d$ denote the space of holomorphic self-maps $f:\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ of algebraic degree $d$, viewed as a finite-dimensional complex manifold parametrized by the coefficients of the homogeneous polynomial representatives (equivalently, an open subset of a projective space of coefficient tuples). An attractive basin of $f$ is the basin of attraction of an attracting periodic cycle of $f$, i.e. a periodic orbit at which the derivative has all eigenvalues of modulus strictly less than $1$, together with all points whose forward orbit converges to that cycle. Equip $\mathcal{H}_d$ with Lebesgue measure (in any coordinate chart of the parameter space).

Question: Does the set of $f\in\mathcal{H}_d$ possessing infinitely many distinct attractive basins have Lebesgue measure zero?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of holomorphic maps of $\mathbb{P}^2$ with infinitely many attracting basins (Newhouse-type phenomena via homoclinic tangencies) is known, but I could not find a definitive published resolution of whether the parameter set of such maps in $\mathcal{H}_d$ has Lebesgue measure zero. The question appears to remain open in this generality.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Hénon maps: real, complex and beyond (BIRS report)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Newhouse phenomena and coexistence of infinitely many sinks in complex/holomorphic dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Mechanisms producing infinitely many attracting basins (via homoclinic tangencies) are established, but measure-theoretic genericity questions remain a topic of active research.
